title: Measure the three arrival-ordered streams and whether they share an order
question: do any two of the three arrival-ordered streams — routerEvents, pendingWorkEvents/the frame's events list, and boundary.entries — carry a comparable field (a timestamp, a sequence number, an arrival index) that would let one merged story be honest?

measuredAt: static: extension/agent-main.js was read line by line at the head above, every citation below was printed from the file with its leading and trailing whitespace trimmed and then re-read, and the three counts in `measurements` were produced by the commands recorded beside them. No page was read, no browser was opened, nothing was rendered and no build was run; the only commands executed were the counting commands in `measurements` and the verify suite at scripts/interaction-story.test.mjs.

measurements.claims: no stream records an interaction; the only click listener in extension/ is the panel's own element picker (overlay.js:507 via attachInput :440), which preventDefaults and locks an element rather than recording a user action

measurements.note: the six listeners extension/agent-main.js registers are the two custom events DI_QUERY_EVENT and PICK_EVENT (:2484, :2489) and the two global error events 'error' and 'unhandledrejection' (:2550, :2557); none of them is a click, pointer, mouse or key listener. Corrected while defining M050: extension/overlay.js DOES register one, at :507 attachInput(window, 'click', onClick, true), through attachInput at :440. It is the panel's element picker — onClick (:356) returns unless armed, then preventDefaults and locks the element — so it selects what to inspect and records no interaction. The count above searched for addEventListener('click' literally and was blind to attachInput, a wrapper; it measured 0 where the truth is 1.

answer.statement: yes, all three streams carry `at`, written by one reader — nowMs() at extension/agent-main.js:728 — as the page's own performance.now() reading taken at receipt (router :1638, work :699, boundary :2073). The same function, in the same realm, answers every entry, and the comment at :726–:727 states that one reader makes these readings and the frame's `startedAt` the same measurement on the same scale. Sorting the union of the three streams by `at` ascending is therefore a measurement rather than an invention. It is also all the record offers: no stream carries a cross-stream sequence number or arrival index (seq/sequence/arrivalIndex occur 0 times in the file), so two entries that share one `at` cannot be ordered from this record, and `at` is the page's own reading, not a wall-clock instant.

tiebreak.statement: no field orders two entries that share an `at`: the only per-arrival number the file records is the router's own navigation id (:1639), which the two route-config classes do not carry and which no work or boundary entry records; the per-frame cycleId (:741) is one value per frame, not one per arrival.

consequence: The narration may interleave the three streams by `at` ascending. It must sort the union of the entries it holds and never concatenate the streams or their per-record copies, because a work entry published in a later frame can carry an earlier `at` (held at :703, adopted at :744) and because routerEvents and boundary.entries are cumulative copies that repeat earlier arrivals.

Two entries with equal `at` are one instant to this record: the narration must render them as simultaneous, or state that the order between them is not recorded. It must never pick a winner from list position, stream order or the router's `id`.

`at` is the page's own clock reading: it may be rendered as the page's own time (milliseconds from performance.now(), with the Date.now() fallback at :735) and must not be rendered as a wall-clock time or a date.

The narration must state that what it merges is bounded: 512 router arrivals (:1471), 64 held work entries (:640) and 128 boundary arrivals (:1939) are kept, and the oldest fall off the front. A merged story orders what the record still holds and never claims completeness.

The merged story narrates what the page emitted and nothing the user did: no stream records an interaction, `interaction` occurs 0 times in extension/agent-main.js and in all 28 extension/*.js files, and no extension file registers a click, pointer, mouse or key listener (measurements.no-ui-capture). A narration that named a user action from these three streams would be inventing it (N3).

notClaimed: No page was read and no browser was opened: every citation in this record was read from extension/agent-main.js as a source file at the recorded head. Nothing was executed against a page, nothing was rendered and no running page's clock was observed, so the statement that the three streams share `at` is a reading of three assignment lines and of the one reader they call, not an observation of three arrivals on one clock.
Nothing here claims what the merged narration will look like or that it exists: the narration is T002 and no file for it exists at this head.

Nothing here claims that the three streams together record what a user did: `interaction` occurs 0 times in extension/agent-main.js and in all 28 extension/*.js files, and no extension file registers a click, pointer, mouse or key listener (measurements.no-ui-capture).

Nothing here claims the streams are complete: the oldest arrivals are dropped above each bound (512 router, 64 held work, 128 boundary), so a merged story can only order the entries the record still holds.

The `at` readings are the page's own clock readings, not wall-clock instants: nowMs() answers performance.now() and falls back to Date.now(), and the entry does not record which of the two answered it.
Nothing here claims a tiebreak between entries whose `at` readings are equal: no stream records a cross-stream sequence number or an arrival index (measurements.no-sequence-field).
verdict: measured: the three arrival-ordered streams do share one comparable field. routerEvents (:1474), the frame's events list built from pendingWorkEvents (:639, :692) and boundaryEntries (:1942) each record `at` from a single reader, nowMs() (:728), as the page's performance.now() reading at receipt (:1638, :699, :2073), so a merged story ordered by `at` is honest. What the record does not offer is a tiebreak — no cross-stream sequence number or arrival index exists in the file — so equal `at` readings are one instant, not an order the narration may choose. The streams are bounded as page-health guards, not curations (512, 64 and 128 kept, oldest dropped), routerEvents and boundary.entries are cumulative copies while the work list is frame-scoped, and no stream records an interaction at all: `interaction` occurs 0 times across extension/agent-main.js and the 28 extension/*.js files. The narration must treat the shared clock as a measurement, the absence of a sequence number as a refusal to order ties, the bounds as an incompleteness it states, and the absence of a user-action stream as a thing it will not invent (SC1, SC3; N3).
